items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had signed a contract with Miriam Burton only for the tour... Miriam knew that she could not be hired for the Chikito, so she sent this girl to see me. Her name was Suzette Aimes... So everything went smooth for a while at the Chikito.

ctx.x: When I was in Geneva with Jack Dieval, I had met a young Swiss drummer called Caspoil whose real name was Pascal Jeanmairet. He had left me use his bicycle during my stay of one month, and I rode it around town most every day. So when I found out that Zutty had left, with the help of my friend Felix Debrit, I was able to get in touch with "Casspoil". He was actually an amateur drummer, but he studied the drums and could play very well. As luck would have it, he was free to join and arrived in Bern that afternoon…

I had signed a contract with Miriam Burton only for the tour because I knew that she was not the kind of singer for a night-club. Miriam knew another American Negro girl that was in Paris with her sister. Miriam knew that she could not be hired for the Chikito, so she sent this girl to see me. Her name was Suzette Aimes. Suzette had a very nice low voice and her approach to singing jazz was quite new and could be compared with the way some of the girls are singing today such as Aretha Franklin, etc. But she was…

The replacement for Dickie Wells was Benny Waters whom I had worked with in Charlie Johnson's orchestra. He had come to Switzerland with Jimmy Archey, the band that Tommy Benford was coming to Europe with after I had arranged with him to make the tour with me. This orchestra was very badly handled by whoever the agent was that had them to come to Europe and after a very few concerts, they all went back to New York, except Benny.
